title: Goodbye Crater Lake, So Long Trillium Lake: Between Eugene And Klamath Falls Is An Alpine Lake To Camp And Fish - NewsBreak
text:
By Editor recommendations ,
1 days ago Crater Lake's pristine alpine scenery and deep blue water make it a beautiful setting for trout fishing, mountain hikes, or sleeping under the stars. But those impressive views and wealth of outdoor activities also make it a very popular destination. According to the National Park Service (via OregonLive), more than 630,000 people visited Crater Lake in 2025, and it's particularly bustling from June through September. Trillium Lake in Mt. Hood National Forest offers similarly stunning scenery, along with fishing and family-friendly camping, but it too sees hundreds of thousands of visitors every year. In fact, summers are so packed that a shuttle service was discussed in 2026 to alleviate congestion in the campground parking area. For travelers who don't want to contend with crowds, there's another lake in Oregon to consider: Timpanogas Lake, a remote destination hidden within the Willamette National Forest about 50 miles north of Crater Lake.
